_subtopic_comment: English and Verbal Reasoning subtopics may be written either way round:
the Title Case name shown here, or the snake_case slug from the schema
('literal_retrieval'). Both resolve to the same subtopic on import.
'question_type' is the third level and is required for ENG, MAT and VR.
Both names come from taxonomy.json and are matched character for character.
questions.passage: Put the shared reading passage here. Several questions may repeat the same passage text — that is fine and expected. Leave this as "" (or omit it) for questions that stand alone.
questions.stem: Write the actual question the student answers here. This field is required.
_options_comment: Four or five options are both fine — there is no cap. Real GL comprehension
sections use five (A-E), so five is shown here; other sections often use four.
Note where the correct answer sits: THIRD, not first. Nothing forces the key
to the top of the list, and a pack that always puts it there teaches a pupil
to pick A without reading. The validator warns about a run of four or about
more than half a pack landing in one position, but the habit is easier than
the warning: vary it as you write.

options.text: The correct answer. Exactly one option must have correct: true.
A fifth distractor — comprehension questions usually offer five.

questions.explanation: Optional but strongly encouraged: why the correct answer is right. Shown to the student after they answer. Leave as "" or omit if you have none.

questions._subtopic_comment: Written as a slug this time, to show both forms work.
questions.stem: Which word is closest in meaning to 'reluctant'?
questions.explanation: Explain the answer in a sentence a Year 5 or 6 pupil would follow.

_comment: NOT part of the pack — the importer and validator ignore keys starting with '_'.
Maths is the one section whose taxonomy has been rebuilt, so a MAT question
needs a 'question_type' as well as a 'subtopic'. Both names come from
taxonomy.json and are matched character for character.
Three shapes below: multiple choice, numeric entry, and short text.

multiple_choice.stem: Sam drives 90 km in 1.5 hours, then a further 60 km in 1 hour. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
multiple_choice.explanation: Total distance 150 km over a total time of 2.5 hours: 150 ÷ 2.5 = 60 km/h. It is not the average of the two speeds.

_comment: The pupil types the number. No 'options'. Units go in 'unit', which is
shown beside the box, NOT inside 'answer' — "5.75" is right, "£5.75" is not.
'also_tests' records the second subtopic this really needs: the money
context is the question, but the arithmetic is where pupils lose the mark.
numeric_entry.stem: Sara buys 3 books at £4.75 each. She pays with a £20 note. How much change does she receive?

_comment: A typed word or short phrase. List every spelling you would accept in
short_text.explanation: An angle greater than 180° but less than 360° is reflex.
